properties.name: Dean's House
properties.date_src: first documented 1515 (Gavin Douglas installed in the Dean's house); medieval origin per HES listing; remodelled c.1715
properties.notes: CONJECTURAL pre-1715 form: the c.1715 house without the later dormers and porch, natural (buff) harl. The earlier building's real form is not documented.

properties.name: Rectory House
properties.date_src: HES listing LB5640 / Wikipedia: completed c.1715; dormers and wooden porch added later (undated, shown throughout)
properties.notes: 2 storeys over a basement, five-window harled front with stone margins, square rear stair tower, later dormers and wooden porch. Natural (buff) harl until the walls were painted white (date assumed, not sourced).

properties.name: Rectory House
properties.date_src: white walls as at present; the date of the change is an assumption
properties.notes: Same model as rectory_house with white-painted harl. The change-over year is an ASSUMPTION; adjust from_year/to_year of this entry and the one before.

properties.name: Dunkeld and Birnam Community Co-Working Space
Bishop's Palace
properties.notes: CONJECTURAL form: tower house (SW), hall range with forestair and crow-stepped gables, walled close with gate. Documented: 1408 tower house, great hall with vaulted granaries/larder, burnt 1689; appearance otherwise inferred. Slezer 1693 view not consulted.

properties.name: Old Dunkeld House Palace
properties.notes: Form follows the Slezer 1693 view as described on stravaiging.com: rectangular block, 3 storeys + attic, corner bartizans, one dormer per side, flat roof with two chimney blocks and a central onion-domed tower. Bay spacing, door position, finishes and colours are inferred.

properties.name: Old Dunkeld House (earlier house)
properties.date_src: HES leaflet: Dean's Manse became the Earl of Atholl's residence in 1566; blown up 1653
properties.notes: CONJECTURAL. No source describes this house. Tower, stair tower, three-storey hall range and walled forecourt, placed on the same site as Bruce's 1676 house (HES: rebuilt on the original site). Identity and exact location are uncertain: HES says the Dean's Manse became the Earl's residence in 1566; a 2008 survey (T C Welsh) suggests the pre-1653 mansion may have stood east of the cathedral; the surviving Dean's House (Rectory House) is a different, extant building.

properties.name: Old Dunkeld House (ruin)
properties.date_src: taken by storm and blown up 1653/54; Bruce rebuilt 1676-84
properties.notes: CONJECTURAL ruin of the earlier house: roofless, jagged walls, breach assumed at the north-east of the tower, rubble.

CONJECTURAL form: small two-storey rubble lock-up, dressed quoins, barred windows, hipped slate roof, one chimney. No source describes its appearance. Dates 1714-1809 are the OHM tag; Canmore (NSA 1845) says the old prison was removed c.1743 - verify.

properties.name: Palace (Unfinished)
properties.notes: A large country house was under construction for the Duke of Atholl near Bishop's Hill in 1830, but work stopped on his death in that year.

properties.name: Old Bridge
properties.notes: Conjectural reconstruction: timber deck and rails carried on stone piers. A bridge partly of timber and partly of stone is reported as begun in 1469, but its completion is uncertain. The 1430 start date is retained from the supplied GeoJSON.

properties.name: Bishop Brown Bridge
properties.notes: Conjectural seven-span masonry reconstruction. Historical accounts describe a substantial multi-arched stone bridge; the exact span count, dimensions and profile are not known.

properties.name: Bishop Brown Bridge Remains
properties.notes: Interpretive low pile/foundation remnants in the former bridge line, visible after the bridge fell out of use and was demolished. The 1766 account also mentions part of an arch on the north bank; this model intentionally shows only the piles.
